entities.summary: Roger Joseph Ebert was an American film critic, film historian, essayist, screenwriter and author. He wrote for the Chicago Sun-Times from 1967 until his death in 2013. Ebert was known for his intimate, Midwestern writing style and critical views informed by values of populism and humanism. Writing in a prose style intended to be entertaining and direct, he made sophisticated cinematic and analytical ideas more accessible to non-specialist audiences. Ebert endorsed foreign and independent films he believed would be appreciated by mainstream viewers, championing filmmakers like Werner Herzog, Errol Morris and Spike Lee, as well as Martin Scorsese, whose first published review he wrote.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent film critic and advocate for independent cinema, Ebert's influence can be seen in the increased recognition of foreign films at mainstream awards ceremonies, with his support for directors like Werner Herzog contributing to their global success. His writing style also helped popularize film criticism among a broader audience.
